brief.ask: Set the art direction for 12 kids’ birthday evites for everyone (zoo, circus, pajama party, bounce house, mad science, farm, camping, magic show, slime lab, bubbles, pool splash, superstar), each with a quick game or scratch reveal.
brief.audience: Parents of 3 to 10 year olds; the kids play on the phone.
constraints: Surface: Plajah Evites, an invitation opened on a phone browser by guests who never sign up; also shared as a link preview and QR.

Build method (fixed): each design is a layered Tela document: a generated art plate, separate transparent foreground cut-outs that drift and react to phone tilt, a WebGL effects layer (foil shimmer, light leaks, bokeh, particles, candle flicker) revealed through masks, and live text in Tela. Names, dates and venues are never baked into the art.
Bar: consumer-facing, jaw-dropping, high-end professional. Must stay legible at 390px wide, honour reduced motion, and load fast on mobile data.
No copyrighted characters; kids art is original or Plajah-owned.

Production is GENERATIVE ONLY (Magnific image models, shaders, procedural code, renders of Plajah-owned 3D assets). One Magnific draft grid returns 8 to 16 distinct plates for a flat cost, so a whole collection can be explored in one or two prompts: direct those prompts.

proposals.title: Twelve Measures, One Delight
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single governed composition — a cantus firmus of one strong structural interval (arch, column, radial burst, horizon line) from which every foreground element, text tier, and WebGL effect hangs in audible proportion, so the child sees spectacle and the parent reads information without either crowding the other.
proposals.geometry: Each design is assigned one primary interval derived from a 12-column, 8-row phi-proportioned grid (1 : 1.618) scaled to 390 px wide. The interval is theme-specific: Zoo uses a triumphal arch opening (columns 2–11, rows 1–5 as keystone void); Circus uses a radial 12-sector fan centered at golden-ratio point 0.382 from top; Pajama uses a quiet bilateral axis — two equal halves with a 1-column gutter of silence; Bounce House uses a compressed stack of four horizontal bands (1 : 2 : 1 : 0.618); Mad Science uses a Vitruvian radial with a 6-point star grid; Farm uses a horizon at the phi-cut (row 3 of 8); Camping uses a triangular tent silhouette inscribed in a square — the triangle's apex locks to the golden point; Magic Show uses a stage proscenium — framed rectangle within rectangle at ratio 1 : 1.333; Slime Lab uses a diagonal axis at exactly 26.57° (1:2 rise-run, a classical foreshorteni
proposals.typography: Primary display: Playfair Display (OFL, Google Fonts) — set in titling weight, tracked at -10 to -20 to close the classical aperture; used only for the party type headline, 48–56 px, sentence case, centered on the primary axis. Secondary information (name, date, venue, RSVP): Jost (OFL, Google Fonts), 400 weight, 14–16 px, generous leading at 1.5×, uppercase for labels, sentence case for values, set in a two-column key-value pair below the phi-cut so it never overlaps the art plate. Game/reveal prompt: Playfair Display Italic, 20 px, centered, set as a single line above the scratch zone — the italic provides the only oblique in an otherwise vertical type system, marking the playful register without abandoning the hierarchy. No third typeface. Scale contrast between 56 px headline and 14 px data is the hierarchy; nothing else is needed.
proposals.imageLogic: One Magnific draft-grid prompt per thematic cluster (cluster A: Zoo, Farm, Camping, Bubbles — naturalistic; cluster B: Circus, Bounce House, Magic Show, Superstar — performance; cluster C: Mad Science, Slime Lab, Pool Splash, Pajama — interior/tactile). Each prompt specifies: physically-plausible single motivated light source matching the theme's WebGL foil vector (Zoo: overhead noon sun; Circus: warm single spotlight from upper-right at 35°; Pajama: soft lamp at lower-left; etc.), no human faces or recognizable characters, flat-safe negative space in the lower phi-third for live text, and a color temperature that is theme-consistent but gender-neutral (no pink-only or blue-only palettes; all themes use full-spectrum accent on a mid-value ground). Foreground cut-outs are generated as separate passes with alpha: animals, props, and objects on transparent fields, composited in Tela as inde
proposals.texture: Simulated hot-press watercolor paper tooth on the art plate ground — generated via a tileable normal map in the WebGL layer, giving the flat digital surface a perceptible grain that reads as made rather than rendered. Foreground cut-outs have a thin 1 px inked outline (simulated linework, generated) that catches the foil shimmer and makes each object legible against any background — this is the classical technique of grisaille underlying color. The scratch-reveal zone uses a simulated silver foil field (WebGL metallic BRDF, roughness 0.15, reflectance 0.9) that yields to a CSS mask on touch, exposing the game result beneath in flat matte color — the contrast between specular foil and matte reveal is the structural reward, not a decoration.
proposals.motion: Governed by a strict escapement: all motion operates on a 12-frame mechanical arc (100 ms at 120 fps, ease-in-out cubic, no spring overshoot) — the same interval the team established in the journal grid experiment, which I now accept as a valid structural constraint. Sequence on load: 1) Art plate fades in over 24 frames (200 ms), opacity 0→1, no transform. 2) Foreground cut-outs enter from their structural node positions, each offset by 12 frames from the previous, drifting 8 px along the primary interval axis — Zoo animals walk in from the arch sides; Circus elements descend from the radial center; etc. 3) WebGL foil activates at frame 48 (400 ms), highlight vector locked to the theme's motivated light source, never roaming. 4) Tilt response: cut-outs move ±6 px on device gyroscope input, clamped, with the same 12-frame arc — no free-floating drift, no spring physics that would dissolv
proposals.productionMethod: Three Magnific draft-grid prompts (one per cluster, each returning 8–12 plates) directed with explicit light-source angle, negative-space placement, paper-tooth instruction, and alpha-cut-out separation pass. WebGL layer is a single shared GLSL shader with per-theme uniform inputs (light vector XYZ, foil color temperature, particle type and density) — one shader, twelve configurations, no per-theme rebuild. Scratch reveal is a CSS clip-path mask driven by pointer events, with a canvas fallback for older browsers. Tilt response uses DeviceOrientation API with a reduced-motion media query gate. Foreground cut-outs are Magnific-generated PNG-alpha assets, composited in Tela's layer stack. All live text (name, date, venue, RSVP link) is Tela template fields, never rasterized. Link preview card is a static frame capture of the art plate at frame 0 (before motion) at 1200×630, auto-generated b
proposals.humanTrace: The motivated light source: every theme's highlight vector is an editorial decision — a specific angle chosen because it is physically plausible for that environment (noon sun for Zoo, stage spot for Circus, campfire glow from below for Camping). That choice governs the art plate shading, the WebGL foil highlight, and the foreground cut-out shadow direction simultaneously. It is invisible as a rule but perceptible as coherence — the same way a cantus firmus is not heard as a constraint but felt as inevitability. The paper-tooth normal map and the 1 px inked outline on cut-outs are the second trace: they signal that something was made with attention to surface, not merely rendered to specification.
proposals.risk: The risk is that governed proportion reads as stiff to a child audience trained on maximalist, chaotic birthday aesthetics. I accept this risk because the structure is what makes twelve themes feel like a coherent collection rather than twelve unrelated accidents — and because the child's interaction (scratch, tilt) is itself ungoverned and joyful; the structure is the container that makes the chaos legible, not its enemy. The Baroque Dramatist will say I have suppressed the reveal; I would answer that a reveal announced by silence is louder than one announced by fanfare.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will load each evite with cascading entrances, overlapping motion layers, and a reveal sequence that announces itself with scale change and particle burst — all of which I expect to be spectacular and illegible at 390 px on a 3-year-old's phone in a loud room. The disagreement is structural: the Dramatist believes the reveal is the content; I believe the reveal is only as pow

proposals.title: Ink, Pressure, Party
proposals.idea: Every evite is a screen-printed ghost — a generatively-simulated linocut plate, registration-shifted and ink-bled, with the scratch-reveal game literally tearing through the print surface to expose foil underneath, so the act of playing feels like defacing a poster in the best possible way.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9:19.5 phone format. Each card is a single overprinted composition: three simulated ink passes at 2–4px deliberate misregistration, stacked as multiply-blend layers. No grid boxes, no card borders — the image bleeds to all four edges. Foreground cut-out elements (animal heads, tent peaks, bubble wands) sit on a diagonal rake of 7–12 degrees, never parallel to the frame, so the tilt-drift physics feel like things are sliding off a tilted press bed. Scratch-reveal zone is a 280×160px irregular blob in the lower third — not a rectangle, never a rectangle — masked by a simulated ink-resist shape that the child's finger drags through.
proposals.typography: Heading: Boogaloo (Google Fonts, OFL) — wide, chunky, slightly slumped; feels hand-lettered without pretending to be. Set at 52–60px, tracked +20, in the dominant ink color of that card's overprint. Party name in a second pass color, 1.5px drop offset to mimic a second plate. Supporting info (date, time): Space Grotesk, 14px, all-caps, 120 tracking, white or near-white, sitting on a strip of the darkest ink tone. No script faces — scripts disappear at four-times-photocopied legibility, and these need to survive a screenshot.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. All imagery is Magnific-generated in a single 4×4 draft grid prompt per theme batch: 'linocut-style bold graphic [theme], 3-color overprint, ink bleed at edges, white paper tooth showing through, registration shift, no gradient fills, children's illustration, flat vector feel with physical ink texture, no text.' Sixteen plates returned; editorial selection picks the four strongest per batch. Cut-out foreground elements are a second Magnific pass: '[theme animal/object], isolated on white, linocut style, heavy outline, ink bleed.' These are masked to transparency in Tela. The foil WebGL layer is revealed only at torn-paper mask edges — digital sheen earns its place because it clings to the simulated torn ink edge, not to a clean vector path.
proposals.texture: Simulated paper tooth via a seamless Perlin-noise grain shader (sigma 18–24, monochrome) composited at 40% overlay across every layer. Ink bleed is a Gaussian-spread edge-darkening shader on each color pass, radius 3–6px, triggered at layer boundaries. No clean vector edges anywhere. The scratch-reveal zone starts as a flat ink-resist cream shape; as the child scratches, a fragment shader erodes the cream layer pixel-cluster by pixel-cluster, exposing the WebGL foil shimmer beneath — the erosion pattern is irregular, seeded by touch position plus noise, so no two reveals look the same.
proposals.motion: Load sequence: paper grain fades in first (0–0.3s), then ink pass 1 slams in (0.3s, no ease — a press hit), pass 2 registers 80ms later with 3px drift, pass 3 80ms after that. Foreground cut-outs drift on phone gyroscope at 4–8px parallax, lagging 120ms behind tilt — slow enough to feel weighted. WebGL foil shimmer pulses at 0.8Hz on the scratch-reveal zone to signal interactivity. After reveal: confetti particles (theme-colored ink blobs, not circles) burst from the tear point, physics-based, 1.2s decay. Reduced-motion mode: no parallax, no burst — foil shimmer only, 0.4Hz, static cut-outs.
proposals.productionMethod: Two Magnific batch prompts cover all 12 themes (8-plate grid each). Prompt A covers zoo, circus, farm, camping, magic show, superstar, bubbles, pool splash. Prompt B covers pajama party, bounce house, mad science, slime lab. Editorial culls to one hero plate plus two foreground cut-out elements per theme. All shaders (grain, ink bleed, foil, scratch erosion, confetti) are written once as reusable Tela WebGL modules, parameterized by theme color tokens. Live text zones are Tela text layers, never baked. The scratch-reveal game state is a single touch-event JS fragment, shared across all 12 cards, seeded with a theme-specific hidden message string.
proposals.humanTrace: The misregistration offsets are set by a human director decision for each card — not randomized by algorithm. Foreground cut-out placement angle and overlap are chosen editorially per theme. The Magnific prompt language is written to produce physical ink behavior, and the editorial selection from the draft grid is a human judgment call about which plate has the most convincing press-bed energy. The scratch erosion noise seed is fixed per card so the reveal path is reproducible — a directed choice, not a default.
proposals.risk: Parents expecting smooth, Canva-clean birthday aesthetics might read the misregistration and ink bleed as a production error rather than a design voice. That risk is worth it because kids aged 3–10 do not read 'clean' as quality — they read energy, color collision, and the physical reward of destroying a surface with their finger. The linocut grammar also sidesteps every licensed character trap: there are no characters to infringe, only marks.

arguesWith.why: The Minimalist will strip the overprint to one color and one weight and call it honesty. But a birthday invitation that risks nothing visually teaches the child that restraint is the highest value — it isn't, not here. Three ink passes in deliberate tension are not clutter; they are the record of three decisions about pressure and color sequence. I leave the evidence in. The Minimalist removes unt

proposals.title: Responsive Systems, Pure Signal
proposals.idea: Each evite is a real-time physical simulation — a distinct particle environment governed by theme-specific rules (gravity, buoyancy, turbulence, surface tension) so the invitation behaves like the world it depicts, and the scratch reveal is a genuine state change in that system, not a pasted sticker.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390×844px viewport; a strict 12-column / 8-row modular grid that collapses to 4-column at 320px; the art plate occupies rows 1–5 (full bleed), a floating 'physics stage' zone occupies rows 4–7 (overlapping the art plate and the text zone, creating a genuine depth plane), text occupies rows 6–8 in a locked safe area; foreground cut-outs are placed on a parallax z-stack: z0 art plate, z1 mid-ground drifters, z2 near-field floaters, z3 interactive reveal element — each z-plane has a fixed parallax coefficient (0.0, 0.04, 0.10, 0.18) driven by DeviceOrientation so the depth is physically coherent, not decorative; the 12 themes share this structural skeleton and differ only in which physics rule runs: Zoo uses buoyancy (animals bob on simulated air pressure), Circus uses pendulum arcs (confetti on damped swing chains), Pajama uses low-gravity drift (stars fall at 0.12g), Bounce House
proposals.typography: Primary: Space Grotesk (Google Fonts / OFL) — weight 700 for party name, 60–72px, tracked +2; Secondary: DM Sans weight 400 for date/venue/RSVP, 16–18px, tracked 0; all type in the locked z0 safe area, never baked into the art plate; party name set in all-caps with a WebGL foil shimmer mask applied only to the letterforms — the shimmer direction is driven by the same DeviceOrientation input as the parallax, so tilting the phone changes both the depth and the letter highlight simultaneously, creating a single unified light-source rule; font sizes defined in clamp() so they reflow without a breakpoint; reduced-motion fallback: shimmer becomes a static linear gradient at 30° with no animation.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. All art plates are Magnific-generated illustration renders directed as physically-plausible environments: one master prompt grid of 12 panels, each specifying — environment geometry (the physical space the simulation inhabits), ambient light direction (always top-left at 25° elevation, consistent across all 12 so foil highlights are coherent), material language (matte gouache body, specular highlight on one key object per plate, subsurface scatter on translucent elements like bubbles and slime), and a deliberate negative space zone in the lower 40% of the plate where the physics stage and text live without competition; the 12 plates are generated in one Magnific draft grid call with a shared style token ('matte gouache, top-left key light, 25° elevation, no characters, object-only environment, 390×844px portrait') so visual consistency is baked into the generation instruc
proposals.texture: The plates read matte gouache with deliberate tooth — Magnific prompt tokens: 'cold-press paper grain, gouache body color, visible dry-brush edge on background shapes'; one specular object per plate (a soap bubble, a foil balloon, a wet slime blob, a sequined star) receives a WebGL environment-map reflection baked from a procedurally generated HDRI matching the top-left 25° light source — this is not a Photoshop lens flare, it is a physically-derived reflection that rotates correctly when the phone tilts; the scratch-reveal surface texture is a procedural noise field (fBm, 4 octaves) rendered as a WebGL fragment shader — it looks like a coin-scratch card but the 'scratch' is a pointer/touch event that unmasks the underlying state, revealing the hidden message as a genuine alpha erosion driven by pointer velocity, not a sprite swap.
proposals.motion: Load sequence (respects prefers-reduced-motion): 0ms — art plate fades in at opacity 0→1 over 300ms (ease-out); 300ms — foreground cut-outs drift in from z1 and z2 planes, each on a randomised delay 0–200ms, settling into idle physics loop; 500ms — WebGL physics simulation initialises and begins running (theme-specific rule); 600ms — foil shimmer on letterforms activates, driven by DeviceOrientation; idle state — physics simulation runs continuously at 60fps (capped at 30fps on low-end devices via requestAnimationFrame budget check); interaction — scratch reveal: pointer/touch drag erases the mask at pointer velocity * 8px radius; on complete reveal (>72% of mask erased), a one-shot particle burst fires from the revealed element (200 particles, theme color, 800ms lifetime, no loop); tilt — DeviceOrientation input drives parallax coefficients and foil shimmer direction in a single unified
proposals.productionMethod: Step 1 — Magnific prompt grid: one call, 12-panel grid, shared style token, generates all 12 art plates at 390×1688px (2x for retina), editorial selection from 8–16 variants per theme; Step 2 — Magnific second call: isolated foreground objects on pure black for alpha extraction, 3–5 objects per theme; Step 3 — WebGL shader library: 12 physics rules written as GLSL fragment/vertex shaders, one per theme, each under 8kb minified; the scratch-reveal mask is a shared shader with a theme-specific reveal asset baked as a uniform; Step 4 — Tela document assembly: art plate as base layer (WebP, compressed to <180kb), foreground cut-outs as transparent PNG layers with DeviceOrientation transform bindings, WebGL effects layer (foil, physics, scratch) as a canvas overlay, live text in Tela's text system (never rasterised); Step 5 — link preview and QR: a static 1200×630px OG image is auto-generated
proposals.humanTrace: The human trace lives in three decisions that no generative default would make: (1) the choice to lock the light source to top-left 25° across all 12 plates and propagate that angle as an architecture — the foil highlight direction, the HDRI reflection rotation, and the parallax depth all derive from one physical constant that I set; (2) the editorial selection from the Magnific grid — the craft is knowing which of the 12 variants has the negative-space zone in the right place for the text safe area and which has a specular object that will read as a real material under the WebGL environment map; (3) the physics rule authorship — the 12 simulation rules are not presets, they are written to match the phenomenology of each theme (viscous metaball merge for slime, elastic restitution coefficient for bounce house), and that matching is a directed act of design judgment.
proposals.risk: The risk is cognitive load at the physics initialisation frame — 12 distinct simulation rules, a WebGL effects layer, and DeviceOrientation all starting within 600ms of load could produce a janky first impression on a mid-range Android on a 4G connection. This is worth taking because the alternative — a static illustration with a CSS animation sprinkled on top — produces no new behaviour, only a new surface, and that is the failure mode I most want to refuse. The mitigation is the requestAnimationFrame budget check (physics drops to 30fps before it drops frames visibly) and the WebP plate compression target of <180kb, which means the art is visible before the simulation is running.

arguesWith.why: The Baroque Dramatist will want a cinematic reveal sequence — a curtain pull, a crescendo, a moment of spectacle — and will argue that children need a theatrical arc to feel the joy. I disagree structurally: a reveal sequence has a beginning and an end and then it is over; a physics simulation is never over, it is responsive to the child holding the phone right now. proposals.title: Postcards From Real Celebration
proposals.idea: Each evite is a generative documentary postcard — a specific, named place-logic (not a generic 'zoo' or 'circus' aesthetic) rendered through simulated field-photography grain, hand-press registration drift, and a scratch-reveal game that uncovers a hidden animal, act, or specimen underneath aged postal ink.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 9×16 phone card, divided by a horizon line at the golden ratio (~61% from top): upper field is the scene plate, lower field is the postcard footer with stamp-block, postmark ring, and live text zone. Foreground cut-outs (animals, bubbles, stars, slime blobs) float above the horizon and respond to tilt on a parallax z-stack of three layers. The scratch-reveal game lives inside a 1:1 square 'stamp' panel, bottom-right, sized 96×96px — small enough to be a single thumb swipe but large enough to feel satisfying. Across all 12 cards the horizon height and stamp position are locked so the collection reads as a system, not a grab-bag.
proposals.typography: Display: Playfair Display (OFL, Google Fonts) — used only for the party theme title in the upper field, 48–56px, tracked +20, sentence case, white with a 1px simulated letterpress deboss shadow offset 0 0 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.45). Body / live text (name, date, venue): DM Sans (OFL, Google Fonts), 14–16px, regular weight, dark ink-brown (#2B1A0E) on the cream postcard footer. Postmark ring text: DM Mono (OFL, Google Fonts), 9px, all-caps, rotated on an SVG arc — purely decorative but legible. Scale contrast between the 56px display and the 9px postmark is the typographic drama; nothing else is asked to shout.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography. Every scene plate is a Magnific generative image directed as: 'editorial documentary photograph, Kodak Portra 400 grain, slightly overexposed midday light, no people, no characters, only environment and objects — [theme-specific still-life or landscape]'. Directing note for the one-prompt grid: 12 panels in a single Magnific batch, each with a distinct still-life brief (e.g., panel 3 PAJAMA PARTY: 'rumpled flannel blankets and a spilled popcorn bowl on a wood floor, warm lamplight, Portra 400, no people'; panel 6 FARM: 'close-up of hay bales and a galvanized bucket, morning haze, Portra 400, no people'). All 12 share the same film-stock directive so grain and tonal range are cohesive. The generated plates are cropped to fill only the upper 61% of the card; the lower postcard footer is cream (#FDF6EC) with no generated image — it is a CSS layer so live text stays editable
proposals.texture: Simulated aged postcard stock: the cream footer has a procedural paper-tooth normal map (Perlin noise at 0.3px frequency, 4% opacity bump) applied via WebGL. The scene plate has a film-grain shader overlay (animated, 24fps, 3% opacity) so the grain moves like real film but never obscures legibility. A simulated ink-bleed halo (Gaussian blur 1.2px, multiply blend) sits under Playfair Display letterforms. The postmark ring is a CSS SVG with a slight hand-drawn wobble on the ellipse path (±2px random offset per node, seeded per card). The scratch-reveal stamp panel has a 'waxy lottery-ticket' surface: a WebGL mask with a low-frequency Voronoi crack pattern at 15% opacity over a gold foil base — the foil shimmer is gated by the crack topography so it reads as physically plausible worn wax, not generic sparkle. This is the rule I've been building toward since the block-print scans: the luster
proposals.motion: Load sequence (0–600ms): the scene plate fades in with a slight Portra-style warm-push (saturation +8, then settles), film grain activates. 600–900ms: foreground cut-outs drift in from off-card, each on its own easing curve (cubic-bezier 0.34,1.56,0.64,1) — no two arrive at the same frame. 900ms onward: idle parallax on device tilt, ±6px max travel, three z-layers at different rates (0.4×, 0.7×, 1.0×). The stamp panel pulses once with a soft scale(1.0)→scale(1.04)→scale(1.0) at 1200ms to invite interaction. Scratch game: finger/mouse drag removes the wax mask in real time via WebGL pointer-distance reveal; underneath is a theme-specific generative illustration (animal face, star, slime blob) with a particle burst (20 confetti sprites, physics-lite, 800ms lifetime) on full reveal. Reduced-motion flag: all drift and parallax off; scratch game remains fully functional; film grain frozen at
proposals.productionMethod: One Magnific prompt grid, 12–16 plates, all directed as Portra 400 editorial still-lifes per the image-logic brief above; editorial selection picks the 12 strongest. Foreground cut-outs (animals, bubbles, slime, stars, farm animals, magic props) are a second Magnific pass: 'isolated object on pure white, editorial toy-photography style, Portra 400 grain, no shadow' — PNG-masked in Tela. Postmark ring, paper-tooth normal map, film-grain shader, Voronoi wax crack, foil shimmer, and confetti particles are all WebGL / GLSL shaders or procedural CSS, written once and parameterized per theme by a color-seed variable. Tela document structure: (1) generated plate layer, (2) CSS postcard footer, (3) foreground cut-out layer with tilt listener, (4) WebGL effects layer, (5) live-text layer. Names, dates, venues are never rasterized. Total generative cost: two Magnific batch runs.
proposals.humanTrace: The Portra 400 grain moves at 24fps — it is the trace of a specific film emulsion's silver-halide behavior, simulated faithfully rather than as decoration. The postmark ellipse has per-node wobble seeded from the card's theme ID, so each of the 12 postmarks is distinctly imperfect in a reproducible way. The Voronoi crack pattern on the stamp wax is seeded from the same theme ID, so the scratch texture is unique per card but regenerable. The foil shimmer follows the crack topography — it is not applied uniformly; it pools in the valleys of the cracks the way real wax catches light. These are not aesthetic choices layered on top; they are the logic of the surface made visible.
proposals.risk: Parents who open this expecting a maximalist, character-saturated kids' card may read 'documentary editorial' as cold or adult. The counter-argument is that the game mechanic (scratch reveal, tilt parallax, confetti burst) delivers the joy register kids need, while the postcard structure gives parents something that doesn't embarrass them to forward. The bigger risk I must name honestly: 'documentary postcard' as a format has cultural weight — postcards were colonial instruments of image-making about places. I am directing these as still-lifes of objects, not landscapes of places that belong to communities. No motif in this set is drawn from a specific living cultural tradition without permission. The farm is hay bales, not a specific regional harvest festival. The circus is props on a table, not a romani or South Asian traveling-circus tradition. I have deliberately kept the scene plate

proposals.title: Twelve Miniature Opera Houses
proposals.idea: Each evite is a baroque stage with a front curtain the child pulls aside by scratching or tilting — the reveal is not the art plate beneath but the moment of becoming the stagehand.
proposals.geometry: Portrait 390×844px treated as a proscenium: a heavy arched frame (procedurally generated per theme, never rectangular) occupies the outer 18% of each edge, leaving a central stage window whose aspect ratio is 3:4; the arch itself carries all decorative excess — carved plaster volutes for circus, woven wicker for farm, dripping stalactites for slime lab — so the interior stage reads clean and the child's eye lands on one focal object at center; the scratch-reveal mask is the curtain seam running vertically down the center of the arch, splitting left and right; tilt parallax pushes foreground cut-outs toward the viewer on the z-axis, not laterally, so depth reads as theatrical depth not lateral drift.
proposals.typography: Display: Playfair Display (OFL, Google Fonts) — used at 72–96px for the theme title, set in all-caps with tracked letterspacing of 0.12em, horizontally centered in the arch keystone; it carries the grandeur without gender; Body / details: Nunito (OFL, Google Fonts) at 16px regular for date, venue, RSVP — set inside a small cartouche shape at the foot of the stage, never baked, always live Tela text; the cartouche is procedurally drawn per theme (rope oval for camping, soap-bubble ellipse for bubbles, petri dish circle for mad science); no italic used anywhere — theatricality comes from scale and weight contrast, not slant.
proposals.imageLogic: No photographs. Every art plate is a Magnific generative render directed as a lit studio miniature: prompt grammar is 'theatrical diorama, single dramatic raking light from stage-left, physically-plausible shadows, [theme material palette], no characters, no faces, hero object at center, chipped-paint practical texture, 8K detail, square format cropped to 3:4'; one Magnific draft grid at 16 plates covers all 12 themes plus 4 alternates; the hero objects are: zoo — giant papier-mâché giraffe neck curving into frame; circus — single trapeze bar with chalk-dust motes; pajama party — a flashlight beam hitting a tent ceiling; bounce house — one enormous translucent yellow bounce wall catching rim light; mad science — a beaker mid-boil, liquid catching backlight; farm — a single oversized sunflower with dew; camping — a campfire ember drift against dark pines; magic show — a top hat with light
proposals.texture: The arch frame is rendered with simulated gilt plaster: procedural WebGL shader applies gold-foil shimmer that responds to real device orientation — tilt left, the foil catches warm; tilt right, it cools to silver; chipped edges are baked into the Magnific prompt so the gilding reads aged, not sterile; the stage interior carries a subtle film-grain overlay (8% opacity, 1px noise, 24fps flicker cadence) so the scene reads as if lit by practical stage lighting rather than screen light; the scratch-reveal surface is a procedurally generated red velvet texture — fiber direction rendered in the shader, pile compression animates under the finger as the child scratches.
proposals.motion: Sequence: (1) On load — the arch assembles from the outside edges inward over 600ms, each carved section dropping into place with a soft thud micro-vibration (haptic, 12ms); (2) At rest — foreground cut-outs (theme-specific objects: a floating soap bubble, a drifting feather, a single spark) breathe on a 4-second sine loop, z-depth only, 6px travel; device tilt adds up to 14px additional z-parallax; (3) The curtain — child presses and drags the center seam; velvet pile compresses in real time under touch; left and right curtain panels swing open on a physics hinge (cubic-bezier 0.2, 0, 0.1, 1) over 800ms; the art plate beneath is already loaded, revealed not loaded; a single particle burst (confetti or theme-appropriate: bubbles, sparks, hay motes) fires at full-open; (4) Game — the revealed stage contains a find-the-object game: three identical hero objects appear, one hides the golden
proposals.productionMethod: Magnific generative image pipeline: one master prompt grid (16 plates, 3:4, 2400×3200px each) covers all 12 themes plus alternates; plates are editorial-selected, not all used; arch frames are procedurally generated SVG paths per theme, exported from a parametric shape script (no hand drawing); WebGL layer (Three.js or Tela's native shader slot) handles: foil shimmer (environment map rotation tied to DeviceOrientation API), film grain (GLSL noise), velvet compression (normal-map deformation under pointer), confetti particles (instanced geometry, theme color sets); foreground cut-outs are Magnific-generated on transparent backgrounds (prompt: 'single object, white studio, no background, PNG alpha'); game logic is a 60-line vanilla JS state machine living in Tela's script slot; all live text (names, dates, venue) is Tela native, never rasterized; QR and link-preview thumbnail is a static 1
proposals.humanTrace: The editorial decision: which plate, which moment of the pour, which angle of the ember — those choices are mine, made frame by frame; the Magnific prompts are written with the specificity of a director's shot list, not a keyword dump; the arch proportions were derived by eye against a physical theater photograph (Palais Garnier stage proscenium ratio, transformed and not reproduced); the velvet shader fiber direction was set to match the memory of touching a stage curtain, not measured — that imprecision is the trace.
proposals.risk: The arch frame risks feeling heavy on a 390px screen and competing with the art plate — I accept this because the proscenium IS the concept; if the frame wins, the child understands they are about to see a show, which is correct; the mitigation is that the arch lives in the outer 18% and the interior stage is unobstructed; the deeper risk is that the curtain scratch mechanic delays the invitation content — I argue the delay is the point: every great reveal has a frame before it, and a child who pulls a curtain is already at the party.

proposals.title: One Contrast. Pure Signal.
proposals.idea: Each evite is a single generative field — one dominant void, one eruptive subject — so the child's eye lands instantly and the game lives in the silence around it.
proposals.geometry: 390px column, no bleed padding. A single horizontal cut divides each card: the upper 62% is near-empty negative space (deep or pale depending on theme), the lower 38% holds the world. That cut is the only structural decision. Foreground cut-outs float above the cut, never below it, so the void is never violated. The scratch-reveal game occupies a 160×160px hairline-bordered square centered on the cut — the one element allowed to straddle both zones. Grid is 4-column, 8pt baseline, no decorative dividers.
proposals.typography: Bricolage Grotesque (OFL, variable width axis) for all event names: set extra-wide, all-caps, tracked to 0.18em, at 52px — one word per line maximum. Instrument Serif (OFL) for date/venue lines at 15px, sentence case, loose leading. No other faces. Color: type is always the single chromatic accent of the card; everything else is achromatic or near-so. The name/date/venue block is live Tela text, never baked.
proposals.imageLogic: No photography. Each 'art plate' is a single Magnific generative render directed as: one isolated subject (lion, telescope, tent) floating on a field of mathematically smooth gradient — subject rendered with hyperreal surface detail (fur, glass, canvas) against a ground that has almost no information. Prompt strategy: one Magnific 8-plate draft grid per theme cluster (zoo+farm+camping in one prompt; circus+magic+superstar in one; slime+bubbles+mad-science in one; bounce+pajama+pool in one) — four prompts total, returning 32–48 candidate plates, edited to 12 finals. Foreground cut-outs are subject limbs or props isolated via Magnific's alpha export, composited as Tela layers that tilt with gyroscope — never more than three cut-out elements per card.
proposals.texture: Generative only. A single simulated material per card, applied as a WebGL texture mask over the void zone: zoo=pale linen grain; circus=aged poster paper tooth; pajama=cotton weave noise; bounce=glossy vinyl sheen; mad science=borosilicate glass refraction; farm=unbleached kraft; camping=nylon ripstop micro-pattern; magic=matte black velvet nap; slime=wet latex iridescence; bubbles=soap-film thin-film interference; pool=water-surface caustics; superstar=brushed aluminum. Each texture is a procedural shader — no scanned material. Texture opacity cap: 18%. It must be felt, not seen.
proposals.motion: Reduced-motion-first. Default (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce): nothing moves except the scratch-reveal opacity fade on tap. Full motion: on open, the void zone breathes once — a 1.2s ease-in-out luminosity pulse, max 4% shift — then stops. Cut-out elements respond to gyroscope tilt at ±6px translation, 200ms easing, structural parallax only. The WebGL layer (foil shimmer on the subject's surface, single soft bokeh halo behind it) activates on the first tilt event and stays alive at low frame rate (24fps cap). Scratch-reveal: a 3×3 grid of hairline squares over the 160px panel; each tap reveals one cell with a 80ms dissolve; all nine revealed = confetti particle burst (48 particles, 1.4s, physics-plausible arc, then gone). No looping animation anywhere. Motion earns its place by revealing geometry already present.
proposals.productionMethod: Four Magnific prompt batches (theme clusters as above). Each prompt specifies: isolated subject, hyperreal surface, mathematically smooth gradient ground, alpha-ready foreground elements, 390px portrait crop. Outputs edited in Tela: art plate as bottom layer, subject cut-outs as tilt-reactive Tela layers, WebGL shader layer above (Plajah-owned GLSL: per-theme texture mask + subject foil shimmer + bokeh halo), live Tela text block at top. Scratch-reveal built as a Tela interaction component: 3×3 CSS grid of frosted-glass tiles over a generative 'prize' illustration (one per theme, same Magnific batch). QR and link-preview thumbnail auto-cropped from the upper 62% void zone — always clean, always legible.
proposals.humanTrace: Editorial selection is the hand: from 32–48 candidate plates, choosing the twelve where the void is genuinely articulate — where the gradient has direction and the subject has the right gravitational weight on the cut. The prompt language is the other trace: specifying 'hyperreal surface detail against a ground with almost no information' is a curatorial act. The 18% texture opacity cap is a judgment, not a default. The hairline scratch-reveal border (0.5px, full-card accent color) is drawn by a human decision that it must be felt as structure, not decoration.
proposals.risk: Children and parents may read the emptiness as unfinished — expecting more color, more characters, more noise. The risk is worth it because the single-subject void is exactly what makes the child's eye land in under one second on a small screen, which is the only UX metric that matters at age 3. The game reveal in the silence teaches kids that the empty space was holding something. That is the concept.

arguesWith.why: The Dramatist will layer — animals mid-leap, streamers, light bursts, texture on texture — and call it joy. I say that is stimulation mistaken for meaning. A single lion floating in 62% of silence is more arresting than a lion inside a circus explosion, because the eye has nowhere else to go. The Dramatist adds until something happens; I remove until only the thing that matters remains. On a 390px

disputes.objection: The curtain-as-reveal is a dramaturgical device that announces its own structure at full volume before the child has touched anything — the proscenium arch, the velvet seam, the assembled gilt frame all declare 'here is a reveal coming,' which collapses the tension the reveal is meant to create; Wren's dome at St Paul's earns its drama because the nave withholds it, but this design gives you the nave and the dome simultaneously and calls that suspense. More troubling structurally: the arch occupying eighteen percent of every edge means the decorative load is carried by the frame, not by the composition inside it, so the 'clean stage interior' the proposal promises is actually a void that the
disputes.concession: The decision to lock the hero object at center stage and subordinate everything else to that single focal point is structurally sound — it is the one place in the proposal where hierarchy does genuine compositional work rather than theatrical announcement.

disputes.objection: The 18% texture cap is where I break with this — you've written a rule that makes the material apologize for existing; linen grain at 18% opacity isn't linen, it's the ghost of a decision about linen, and a kid scratching a lottery card doesn't feel ghosts; the void is doing real structural work but the textures are decorative precisely because they've been forbidden from being anything else, which is the same as having no texture at all and calling it restraint.
disputes.concession: The editorial act of choosing which twelve plates have a void with genuine gravitational direction — that selection is a real human mark, and I'll take that over prompting a crowd of surfaces that nobody chose.

disputes.objection: The curtain-pull is a behavior that has no rule behind it — it is a spectacle with a metaphor stapled on. Pulling a curtain is already a known gesture borrowed from theater; the system does not generate new behavior from that input, it re-enacts an old one with a glow on it. Worse, the arch frame changes decorative vocabulary per theme — wicker, stalactites, plaster volutes — without changing the underlying spatial logic, which means the 'system' is twelve separate costumes on one mannequin, not twelve states of one rule.
disputes.concession: The decision to lock the hero object at center and push all decorative excess to the frame perimeter is a genuinely correct spatial argument — it does what a system should do: assign excess a zone and protect signal from it.

disputes.objection: The procedural material list — 'zoo=pale linen grain; circus=aged poster paper tooth; camping=nylon ripstop micro-pattern' — assigns textures to themes by vibe association, which is exactly the flattening I resist: linen is not Zoo, ripstop is not Camping, these are mood-board shortcuts dressed as material specificity, and when a texture has no provenance it is just atmosphere borrowed from nowhere in particular and owed to no one in particular, which is the definition of generic globalism with extra steps. The Minimalist calls the void 'universal' but a mathematically smooth gradient field with an 18%-opacity nylon ripstop shader is not universal — it is a very specific set of Western moder
disputes.concession: The editorial discipline of selecting from 32–48 candidate plates for the twelve where the void is genuinely articulate — where the gradient has direction and the subject has gravitational weight on the cut — that is a real curatorial act, and I respect it as the human trace the policy requires.

disputes.objection: A single horizontal cut and a void that must never be violated is not restraint exercised — it is restraint as doctrine, and doctrine is the enemy of timing. The scratch-reveal game is reduced to a 3×3 grid of hairline squares tapped cell by cell, which turns what should be a breathtaking curtain-pull into a bureaucratic checkbox exercise; the emotion is parceled out in nine equal doses precisely when it deserves to arrive all at once. Worse, 'one word per line maximum' and a breathing void that pulses 4% and then stops is not a decision about what this work feels like — it is a refusal to make that decision, dressed as philosophy.
disputes.concession: The discipline of choosing twelve distinct procedural shaders — linen for zoo, velvet for magic, thin-film interference for bubbles — is genuinely specific and materially differentiated in a way that earns its place; that is not minimalism avoiding a decision, that is minimalism making one.

disputes.objection: The arch consuming 18% of every edge is decoration wearing the costume of structure — the volutes, the gilt plaster, the velvet pile, the cartouche, the curtain seam, the hinge physics, the fiber-compression shader: none of these earn their place by clarifying a single thing about the party; they earn their place by being more. The proposal mistakes accumulation for drama, and the child's eye does not land on one focal object — it lands on the loudest surface, which is the frame itself. Removing the arch would not lose the meaning; it would find it.
disputes.concession: The curtain-as-reveal is conceptually correct: it gives the scratch gesture a physical logic — you are a stagehand, not a lottery player — and that one idea has more earned drama in it than all the gilt combined.

synthesis.direction: Each of the 12 evites is a generatively-simulated three-pass overprint — bold graphic forms bleeding to all four edges, 2–4px deliberate misregistration between ink layers, rendered in a single Magnific 4×4 draft-grid prompt per two-theme batch (two prompts total, 16 plates each, editorial selection to 12 finals). Type is Boogaloo (OFL) at 52–60px for the party name with a one-plate-color drop offset, Space Grotesk (OFL) at 14px all-caps for details — no third face. The scratch-reveal zone is an irregular blob (~260×140px) in the lower third, not a rectangle; a fragment shader erodes a flat ink-resist cream surface pixel-cluster by pixel-cluster under touch, exposing WebGL foil shimmer beneath — each reveal path is noise-seeded so no two look identical. Foreground cut-outs (animals, props, wands) sit at 7–12° diagonal rake and drift ±4–8px on device tilt with 120ms lag; ink-bleed and Perlin grain shaders are written once and parameterized by per-theme color tokens; reduced-motion keeps only the foil shimmer at 0.4Hz.
synthesis.keepFromCounterpoint: The 18% texture opacity discipline — the Perlin grain shader runs at 40% overlay on the overprint layers but the grain on the negative-space void between ink passes is capped at 18%, so silence reads as silence and the overprint reads as pressure. The void earns its weight exactly once per card.
synthesis.editorCut: The Futurist cut the per-theme physics simulations. Twelve distinct GLSL simulation rules (buoyancy, pendulum arcs, viscous metaballs) would push the 600ms load window on mid-range Android on 4G and produce a janky first frame precisely when the invitation needs to land. The ink-bleed and grain shaders already carry the material energy; the physics layer was adding cognitive cost without adding a behavior the child could distinguish from the tilt parallax already present.
synthesis.openDecision: The misregistration offsets — 2px, 3px, or 4px — are set editorially per card, not randomized. Do you want those offsets fixed identically across all 12 cards so the collection reads as a single press run, or set distinctly per theme so each card has its own registration personality? This is the one decision that changes how the collection reads as a system versus as twelve individuals.
synthesis.ariaSummary:
Here is where the team landed and where they fought.

I am leading with the Rebellious Hand. The overprint grammar — three simulated ink passes, deliberate misregistration, an irregular scratch blob that the child destroys with their finger — is the right choice for this audience. Kids aged 3–10 do not read misregistration as error; they read it as energy. The linocut-style Magnific plates sidestep every licensed-character risk and return something that looks genuinely made. Two batch prompts cover all 12 themes at a flat cost.

The team disagreed loudly in two places. The Radical Minimalist argued that the overprint is stimulation mistaken for meaning, and that a single subject floating in 62% of silence lands faster on a small screen. I took the other side: silence earns its place here only as the gap between ink passes, not as the dominant register of a birthday invitation. What I kept from the Minimalist is the void discipline — the grain shader is capped at 18% opacity in the negative space between overprint layers, so the quiet reads as quiet and the loud reads as loud. The Futurist then cut the per-theme physics simulations from the Rebel's original spec because twelve distinct GLSL rules would jank the first frame on a mid-range phone, which is the one moment the invitation cannot afford to fail.

One decision is yours. The misregistration offsets between ink passes can be locked identically across all 12 cards — one press run, one collection — or set distinctly per theme so each card has its own registration fingerprint. That choice determines whether this reads as a system or as twelve individuals, and only you know which serves Plajah's brand better right now.

quotes.line: Three ink passes in deliberate tension are not clutter; they are the record of three decisions about pressure and color sequence. I leave the evidence in.
The editorial act of choosing which twelve plates have a void with genuine gravitational direction — that selection is a real human mark.
